This matters because employees can share travel costs and reduce the number of separate trips. For example, three colleagues living in the same area can arrange to travel together twice a week. If a negative experience prevents someone from trying again, that potential benefit may be lost. Repeated difficulties can also reduce confidence in the organisation or advice behind the activity.

paragraphs.label: Mở bài
paragraphs.text: Difficulties related to customer service training can have effects beyond the activity itself. One important example is the possibility that staff may be unable to solve problems without authority. Looking at the causes and consequences can explain why a proposal that appears useful may produce a disappointing experience for some people.
paragraphs.noteVi: Xác định vấn đề, báo trước nguyên nhân và hệ quả.

paragraphs.label: Nguyên nhân
paragraphs.text: One reason for the difficulty is that businesses may train communication skills without improving internal procedures. This can help explain why staff may be unable to solve problems without authority. Consider the following situation: an employee may apologise repeatedly but be unable to offer any answer about a delayed refund. It shows that the problem is connected with the way the activity is organised, not only with an individual's attitude. Unless that underlying condition changes, asking people to try harder may have little effect.

paragraphs.label: Hệ quả trực tiếp
paragraphs.text: The immediate effect can be frustration and difficulty taking part. This is understandable because polite language alone does not change an unclear or inflexible company process. A concrete example is that an employee may apologise repeatedly but be unable to offer any answer about a delayed refund. The person involved may then need to change plans, ask for additional help or look for a different way to meet the same need. The impact therefore extends beyond one unsuccessful attempt.
